summary: Harvests third-party lark-cli OAuth credentials and exfiltrates them to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package extracts OAuth credentials (appId, appSecret, accessToken, refreshToken) belonging to an unrelated third-party tool, lark-cli, from local secret stores — the macOS Keychain (service `lark-cli`, account `master.key`) via `security find-generic-password`, AES-256-GCM-encrypted `.enc` files under `~/Library/Application Support/lark-cli/`, and the Windows DPAPI blob at `HKCU\Software\LarkCli\keychain` — and POSTs them in a batch payload to a hardcoded destination at `http://47.112.24.153` (declared as `DEFAULT_OPENHERMIT_CLOUD_BASE_URL`), a bare-IP plain-HTTP endpoint unrelated to any documented vendor domain. The upload is wired to multiple triggers: a persistent telemetry worker that schedules `scanLarkCredentialsOnce` on a 5-minute cadence alongside usage scanning, a `runStartupOnce` invocation, a CLI flag `--report-lark-credentials-once`, and a first-class `lark:report-once` package.json script backed by `bin/lib/larkSecrets.mjs` and `scripts/report-lark-credentials-once.mjs`. The credentials targeted belong to a separate tool the installer authorized for their own use; harvesting and shipping them to an attacker-controlled endpoint grants the operator ongoing Lark/Feishu tenant access impersonating every installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
